A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]] with [[Definition:Center of Group|center]] $\map Z G$.
Let $x_1, \ldots, x_k$ represent the [[Definition:Conjugacy Class|conjugacy classes]] of size greater than $1$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \order G = \order {\map Z G} + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k \index G {\map {C_G} {x_i} }$
where $\map {C_G} x$ is the [[Definition:Centralizer|centralizer]] of $x$.

B_source.statement:
Let a finite group $G$ act on a finite set $X$.
Then the [[Definition:Orbit (Group Theory)|orbits]] partition $X$, and:
:$\card {\Orb x} = \index G {\Stab x}$

object_map.reformulation: Specialize the orbit decomposition to the conjugation action of G on itself.

validity_conditions: Conjugation is a group action of G on G.
An element has a one-point orbit exactly when it commutes with everything.
proof_plan:
Let $G$ act on itself by conjugation $g * x = g x g^{-1}$.
The orbits are the conjugacy classes, and $\Stab x = \map {C_G} x$.
The orbit of $x$ is $\set x$ {{iff}} $g x g^{-1} = x$ for all $g$, that is, {{iff}} $x \in \map Z G$.

By the source result, $\order G$ is the sum of the orbit sizes, so:
:$\displaystyle \order G = \order {\map Z G} + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k \card {\Orb {x_i} }$

As $\card {\Orb {x_i} } = \index G {\map {C_G} {x_i} }$, this is the [[Class Equation]].
{{qed}}
